clue.text: Poet gets no score with finery

parts.note: in tennis a score of nothing is called love
lace is fine decorative fabric, a kind of finery

explanation.surface: A versifier is rewarded with fancy clothes rather than points.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Lovelace was a seventeenth-century Cavalier poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was an English Cavalier lyricist of the 1600s.

clue.text: Cooper put him before the president

definitions.text: Cooper put him before the president

parts.words: Cooper put him before the president
parts.note: James Fenimore Cooper wrote a novel whose title is this hero's first name followed by the surname of a famous US president

explanation.surface: A man is presented to the head of state by someone called Cooper.
explanation.walkthrough: Cooper's novel is Lionel Lincoln: the hero's name stands in front of Lincoln, the name of the president.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooper's 1825 novel Lionel Lincoln puts the hero's forename ahead of the presidential surname.

clue.text: One learned in scripture may have distant recollection, to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A religious scholar might vaguely remember something long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across haVE DISTant.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vedist is a scholar versed in the Vedas, the Hindu sacred texts.

clue.text: Pinter's was associated with no sound

definitions.text: Pinter's was associated with no sound

parts.words: Pinter's was associated with no sound
parts.note: Harold Pinter's short play of this name was staged as a double bill with his play Silence

explanation.surface: A playwright's work was linked to quietness.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinter's Landscape and Silence were first staged together in 1969; 'no sound' is Silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Landscape is a one-act play by Harold Pinter, paired with his Silence.

clue.text: Pigment slightly modified by novelist

parts.note: Aldous Huxley's first novel takes its title from this paint colour with one letter dropped

explanation.surface: An artist's colour has been tweaked a little by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Huxley's novel is Crome Yellow; adding H gives the name of the pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome yellow is a bright lead chromate paint pigment.

clue.text: Blue engine assembled by clergyman

parts.note: the Rev. W. Awdry, a clergyman, created a blue locomotive character of this name in his Railway Series books

explanation.surface: A clergyman puts together a sad-looking motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a mood, but it is the paint colour of Awdry's engine in the Thomas the Tank Engine books.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Blue Engine is a locomotive in the Rev. Awdry's Railway Series.

clue.text: Spirits of some spirit, say

indicators.note: the word is spoken rather than written, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: gin is a type of alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: Some liquor, for instance, counts as hard drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Djinn are supernatural beings of Arabian folklore, genies.

clue.text: He has a major role in A Well remembered Voice

definitions.text: He has a major role in A Well remembered Voice

parts.words: He has a major role in A Well remembered Voice
parts.note: J. M. Barrie's one-act play A Well-Remembered Voice has a character who holds the army rank of Major

explanation.surface: An actor takes a leading part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major role' reads as 'leading part', but the role is that of Major Armitage in Barrie's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Major Armitage is a character in Barrie's wartime play A Well-Remembered Voice.

clue.text: Aeschylus' suppliant women show sea writer on fateful date

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: Richard Henry Dana wrote the seafaring memoir Two Years Before the Mast
the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was murdered

explanation.surface: Greek tragic heroines display a maritime author on an ominous day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danaids, daughters of Danaus, are the chorus of Aeschylus' The Suppliants.

clue.text: Humdrum, like Capek's life

definitions.meaning: Karel Capek wrote the novel An ... Life

explanation.surface: A dull existence, like that of a Czech writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means unremarkable or commonplace; Capek's novel is titled An Ordinary Life.

clue.text: Philip = steadfast fashionable Thackeray hero

parts.note: firm means resolute and unwavering
in means currently in fashion

explanation.surface: A loyal, stylish man named Philip is a Victorian novelist's protagonist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philip' identifies the hero: Thackeray's The Adventures of Philip follows Philip Firmin.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Firmin is the protagonist of Thackeray's The Adventures of Philip.

clue.text: Work hard on the galleys, perhaps

definitions.text: Work hard on the galleys, perhaps

parts.words: Work hard on the galleys, perhaps
parts.note: galleys are galley proofs, printers' trial sheets, not ships rowed by slaves

explanation.surface: Toil like a rower on an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galleys' suggests oared ships; in printing, galleys are proof sheets to be checked.
explanation.definitionFit: Correcting galley proofs means marking printers' errors before publication.

clue.text: Soothes in The Seven Seas (essays)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these words of the title

explanation.surface: A volume of Kipling calms the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across sEAS ESsays.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or worry is to soothe or relieve it.

clue.text: He wrote of a future for Futurism in Figaro, and manifested it in four volumes

definitions.text: He wrote of a future for Futurism in Figaro, and manifested it in four volumes

parts.words: He wrote of a future for Futurism in Figaro, and manifested it in four volumes
parts.note: the Italian poet whose Futurist Manifesto appeared in the Paris newspaper Le Figaro in 1909

explanation.surface: A writer predicted an artistic movement's future in a French newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti founded Futurism with his 1909 manifesto in Le Figaro.

clue.text: "Grief of my son's exile hath stopp'd her breath", says her husband of this mother

definitions.text: "Grief of my son's exile hath stopp'd her breath", says her husband of this mother

parts.words: "Grief of my son's exile hath stopp'd her breath", says her husband of this mother
parts.note: in the last scene of Romeo and Juliet Romeo's father reports his wife's death with these words

explanation.surface: A husband reports that his wife died of grief over their banished son.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo's mother dies offstage of grief at his banishment in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: A leaf from Debrett?

parts.note: Debrett's Peerage lists people with titles, so any page of it is a page of titles

explanation.surface: A sheet torn from the guide to the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: Debrett's is the British guide to the peerage; a leaf is a page, and the opening leaf of any book carries its title.
explanation.definitionFit: A title page is the leaf at the front of a book bearing its name.

clue.text: Sassoon recorded its journey

parts.note: Siegfried Sassoon's 1928 poetry collection is titled for the travels of this organ

explanation.surface: A poet kept a log of some trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassoon's collection The Heart's Journey traces the progress of the emotional core.

clue.text: Giraudoux madam now lost in XVIeme

indicators.note: the letters are scrambled as if gone astray

explanation.surface: A French lady is bewildered in a Paris district.
explanation.walkthrough: Giraudoux wrote The Madwoman of Chaillot; Chaillot is in Paris's sixteenth arrondissement (XVIeme).
explanation.definitionFit: Giraudoux's play La Folle de Chaillot centres on an eccentric Parisian countess.

clue.text: Duncan's town of the stars, possibly twinned with Los Angeles?

definitions.text: Duncan's town of the stars, possibly twinned with Los Angeles?

parts.words: Duncan's town of the stars, possibly twinned with Los Angeles?
parts.note: Los Angeles is the City of Angels, and a celestial city of the stars would house angels too

explanation.surface: A place full of film stars could pair with Hollywood's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests film actors, but the city is in the sky, where angels dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavenly city is the celestial Jerusalem, home of angels.

clue.text: Irish dramatist right — but not so disciplined as novelist

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was an Irish playwright

explanation.surface: An Irish playwright is correct but less orderly than a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as novelist' adds a second hint: Thornton Wilder was an American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilder is the comparative of wild, meaning less controlled.

clue.text: Tarkington introduces writer with fishing gear

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a rod is used for angling

explanation.surface: An author brings in a scribe carrying angling tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: Penrod is Booth Tarkington's 1914 novel about a mischievous boy.

clue.text: Vanbrugh's assistant peddles Othello?

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them in the street
Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: A dramatist's helper sells Shakespeare's tragedy door to door.
explanation.walkthrough: Vanbrugh is the architect of Blenheim Palace, not the playwright side of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Hawksmoor worked as John Vanbrugh's architectural partner at Blenheim and Castle Howard.

clue.text: Attractive nymph

parts.note: a sea creature of Greek myth who lured sailors with her song

explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens were mythical sea nymphs whose singing drew sailors to wreck.

clue.text: English distance covered by Rousseau

parts.note: a unit of length equal to 1,760 yards

explanation.surface: Rousseau travels across a span of English ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Rousseau's treatise on education is Emile, so its subject is what he covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousseau's Émile is a treatise on education, the topic he wrote about.

clue.text: Cupboard conceals my Lear

indicators.note: the words are disguised, their letters rearranged so as not to be seen

explanation.surface: A cabinet hides a copy of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An almery, or ambry, is an old word for a cupboard or recess.

clue.text: Ordinary chaps and royalty featured by Greek poet

parts.note: men are ordinary males
taken as written
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Common men and a queen appear alongside a Hellenic writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Menander was the Athenian comic dramatist of the New Comedy.

clue.text: Anne Brontë's was a painter

parts.note: the title figure of Anne Brontë's second novel, Helen Graham, earns her living as an artist

explanation.surface: A Brontë sister's subject was an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Brontë's novel is The Tenant of Wildfell Hall; Helen paints for income.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall's heroine Helen supports herself by painting.

clue.text: Miss Dell with leftist king?

parts.note: Ethel M. Dell was a popular romantic novelist
red is a common term for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A lady novelist sides with a socialist monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an Anglo-Saxon English monarch.
